However, in immunocompromised patients (e.g., HIV, organ transplant, biologic therapy), molluscum can present atypically: larger size (>5 mm), numerous lesions (>10–20), extracutaneous involvement, or persistent/progressive disease. More importantly, the differential must be broadened if immunosuppression is present — e.g., cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis, or Kaposi sarcoma may mimic umbilicated or papular lesions.
